props.title: Rango
props.initialSlug: A chameleon becomes an unlikely hero in a desert town

sections.content: **Rango** (2011) revolutionized animated Westerns by embracing surreal darkness and mature themes. Director Gore Verbinski brought his **Pirates of the Caribbean** (2003) flair for adventure while channeling Sergio Leone's spaghetti westerns, particularly **The Good, the Bad and the Ugly** (1966). The film's stunning animation from Industrial Light & Magic marked their first full animated feature, pushing photorealistic textures and lighting to new heights. Its existential story about identity and heroism feels more aligned with **Chinatown** (1974) than typical family fare.

sections.content: The film's distinctive visual style draws from both classic Westerns and Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas-style psychedelia. Like **Mad Max: Fury Road** (2015), it uses desert landscapes to create a heightened reality. The character design, particularly Rattlesnake Jake, echoes the menacing villains of **Once Upon a Time in the West** (1968). ILM's attention to detail - from dust particles to fabric textures - set new standards for computer animation, influencing later works like **The Book of Life** (2014).

Rango's existential themes and meta-commentary on heroism connect it to revisionist Westerns like **Unforgiven** (1992) and **Django Unchained** (2012). The protagonist's journey from fraud to genuine hero subverts traditional Western tropes while paying homage to them. Its environmental message about water rights recalls **Chinatown** (1974), while its surreal sequences and Johnny Depp's performance channel the spirit of **Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas** (1998). sections.content: The film's success helped spark renewed interest in both animated features aimed at mature audiences and modern Westerns. Its influence can be seen in subsequent animated films like **Kubo and the Two Strings** (2016) that push technical boundaries while telling sophisticated stories. The Western elements paved the way for other genre hybrids like **Cowboys & Aliens** (2011) and animated features like **Puss in Boots** (2011).
